node-1.label: Right eye incomplete closure, right nasolabial fold flattening, and right-sided hemiplegia for 24 hours

node-2.label: A 66-year-old man with a 3-year history of hypertension and no history of neurological disorders presented with a 24-hour history of symptoms; he was alert and oriented.

node-3.label: Physical examination showed effacement of the right frontal wrinkle, incomplete closure of the right eyelid, flattening of the right nasolabial fold, muscle strength grade 0/5 in right upper and lower extremities, hypoesthesia on the right side, and a positive right Babinski sign.

why.why: Emergency CT reveals hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and lateral ventricle, directly confirming hemorrhagic stroke. MRI shows no brainstem lesion, and DTI demonstrates a thinner left corticobulbar tract, explaining the right facial and limb deficits. These findings strongly support acute cerebrovascular disease, raising confidence from 0.7 to 0.98.

Emergency CT shows hemorrhage rather than an inflammatory or demyelinating process, and MRI shows no brainstem lesion, directly refuting a brainstem inflammatory/demyelinating lesion. The previous suggestion of brainstem involvement is not supported by imaging, so confidence is lowered from 0.2 to 0.05.

Emergency CT demonstrates acute hemorrhage, and MRI shows no space-occupying mass or abscess. The acute onset and imaging findings are incompatible with a slowly progressive tumor or abscess, so confidence is lowered from 0.1 to 0.02.

node-7.label: Emergency CT shows hemorrhage in left thalamus-radiation crown region and lateral ventricle

node-9.label: DTI demonstrates thinner left corticobulbar tract

node-10.label: Hemorrhagic stroke in the left thalamus-radiation crown region with intraventricular extension

why.why: Emergency CT directly demonstrates hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region with intraventricular extension, and MRI/DTI corroborate the supratentorial localization and explain the right-sided deficits. The radiologist's analysis states that the diagnosis of acute hemorrhagic stroke is established and that all key imaging information is concordant; therefore confidence is raised from 0.95 to 0.98.

attrs.why: The patient has a 3-year history of hypertension, a major risk factor for intracerebral hemorrhage, and the hemorrhage is located in the left thalamus-radiation crown region with intraventricular extension, a pattern commonly seen in hypertensive hemorrhage. Confidence is 0.6 because direct blood pressure measurements and exclusion of other causes such as vascular malformation or coagulopathy are not documented.
